cells.tense: You are standing in the pull of what you want, and your fairness is unforced here.
cells.ask: Say a real yes or no to someone before today ends, once, and let the answer stand without explaining it.
cells.core:
You want something, you know what wanting it costs, and you are willing to pay it without pretending the price isn't there. That isn't calculation. It's an honesty in the body. When someone brings you a story, you take it whole. You know how much is theirs and how much is left over, and you don't make a fuss about the difference.

What this balance feeds next is an ending that's owed. Something has run its course, and you already feel it, and you don't need it to be a tragedy to set it down. There's no list of grievances under this. There's just the quiet work of evening things out, which you do naturally. When you've kept that clean, letting go gets easier, not harder.
cells.sheetLine: You even things out by feel, and the feeling is accurate.
cells.verb: To even the scale, with your body doing the math
cells.place: Where the pull shows you what you want, and the wanting is not the road

cells.tense: You are bracing against a version of this where you end up owing more than you get.
cells.ask: Pick one small imbalance you are tracking and let it stay unbalanced one full day. Write down what you did with the feeling instead.
cells.core:
You are counting. Not the rude kind — the careful kind, the kind that knows who called whom and who paid last and who was forgiven what. You're not wrong about any of it. That's what makes it hard to stop. You can see the whole ledger, and it doesn't quite close, and so you keep your eye on it in case it tilts.

But the fairness has turned into arithmetic. The pull you were following is still there — it's still showing you what you want — and you've been answering it with a column of numbers, braced for a future where you come up short. The piece that's missing is the ability to hold things uneven for a while. Not forcing the column to balance. Holding it, seeing it, letting it sit off by a little.
cells.sheetLine: You are tracking a scale that nobody asked you to keep.
cells.verb: To even the scale, with your body doing the math

cells.tense: You learned at some point that asking for what you were owed was not safe.
cells.ask: Name one small thing you are owed and ask for it plainly. Keep the asking itself separate from whether they say yes.
cells.core:
You take what you get. That's the shape of it. Someone shortchanges you and you don't say a word, not because you can't see it — you see it in the body before anyone else does — but because saying it out loud has felt dangerous, so long that not saying it is just who you are now. You've built a life around being fine with less.

Meanwhile you still want what you want. The pull hasn't moved. It's just harder to look at. The way back in isn't a confrontation. It's small, steady practice on your own — one rehearsal, one sentence out loud to nobody, one plain request — so the asking gets built before it gets used. The point isn't to win. It's to remember that asking was ever allowed.
cells.sheetLine: You stopped asking, and you haven't noticed that you did.

cells.tense: The weighing is already happening, and you are putting it on the other person's side of the table.
cells.ask: Notice one thing you have been quietly counting against someone and say it once, neutral, without a case attached.
cells.core:
You are tallying. Not obviously — no list on the fridge. But you know who has been short with you lately, and you know what you've given them, and there's a small score somewhere in you that keeps updating without your permission. You would not call it a score, honestly. You'd call it being observant.

What's actually running is the same even-handedness you do well everywhere else, just disowned here. The pull you follow — toward what you genuinely want — is pointing at relationships that could be made right, and instead your attention is on the drift. Noticing the drift is the gift. Dressing it up as intuition is the blind spot. If you set down the score for one minute and just said what you notice, that would be the quieter kind of knowing the situation is asking for.
